name: evtx_query
description: Query an EVTX event log and return filtered events with timestamp, event id, channel, computer, provider, EventRecordID and named data fields. A run reports three counts apart: records_examined (every record the reader produced), events_matched (records that parsed and passed every filter) and parse_errors (records or chunk chains that could not be read, with their offsets); an error row is never counted as a match, and a run with any parse error, or whose chunks could not be enumerated to the end, is status partial. Every answer and refusal carries status and status_basis. Every row carries record_offset, chunk_offset, the EventRecordID and record_filetime (the FILETIME in the record header, as a decimal string, with record_time_utc by integer arithmetic) beside the XML's own SystemTime. Filters: event_ids, contains (a substring of the XML as the answer prints it), start_record and end_record, and start_time and end_time (ISO 8601: YYYY-MM-DD then optionally THH, THH:MM, THH:MM:SS or THH:MM:SS.fffffff, and from the hour on Z or an offset such as +03:00; no zone is UTC; a time names the span its precision gives, so a date is the whole day; the SystemTime of each record is converted to UTC ticks and compared as a number; a malformed time, a word such as yesterday, or a range that ends before it starts is refused; a record with no SystemTime is left out of a time range and counted in events_without_time_excluded, and the run is partial). The log is accounted for as a whole: chunks_declared (what the file header says), chunks_read (what the reader gave), bytes_expected and file_bytes; a file shorter than its header says or a reader that gave fewer chunks than declared is status partial with a problem naming both, not a log with no records. The file is read to its end, not to the header's count: a chunk past the declared count that has an ElfChnk signature and passes the chunk-header checks is read (its rows say chunk_beyond_declared: true; chunks_in_file, chunks_read_beyond_declared, header_flags and header_dirty say what the file holds), one that has the signature and fails the checks is a problem, an all-zero slot past the count is free space; a declared chunk with no signature is named and not read. A chunk whose string or template table loops or points outside the chunk is not given to python-evtx (which follows them without end): it is named under chunks_not_read, and whatever else the library does is read under a timer of 8 seconds per chunk, after which the chunk is given up and named; the whole run stops at its own time limit (54 seconds) with status partial, and SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP end it with JSON (status interrupted, exit 128 plus the signal) and a partial_result_file that is named as a partial and is not a result. A file that does not begin with ElfFile, a path that is not a regular file, and an out_file that is not text are refused as JSON. The XML of every match is kept in the result file (JSON Lines), which is mode 0600, is written under a temporary name and placed at the end, and never replaces or truncates an earlier result: a result of the same bytes is named again, and when the name is held by another file the first free -2, -3... beside it is used and result_file_requested says so; its default name is made from the arguments without `contains`, so a needle never reaches a file name. limit is the inline page size. SENSITIVE: event data can hold command lines and text typed into one, which can hold a secret; run it as a job with secret_output: true when the log may. WITHHOLDING (one boundary on every way out). Every key and value of the answer, and every row of every file this tool writes, is judged by the type of the field it fills (channel, computer, provider, EventData names and values, and the XML): a name, path, key or URL is shown as it is only when it fits a plain grammar (a path component by component; GUIDs, SIDs, addresses, 0x numbers, times and hexadecimal ids up to 24 digits are plain), free text has token-shaped runs, user-info, the value after a secret's name, vendor-prefixed tokens, padded base64 and PEM keys withheld, and a second check written apart from the first reads it all once more, the text as the evidence wrote it as well as the text shown (a piece of 12 characters of a secret that two cuts left behind is caught) (a string it replaces makes a complete answer partial and is listed under boundary.replaced_at, by the keys on the way as they are shown or by positions, never by a withheld key). A withheld text is <withheld N characters: reason>. Past the judging time (SEAL_BUDGET, 10 seconds for an answer or a row, and never past the seal stop of the tool, which is 3.5 seconds before its time limit because the string being judged at that point is finished first and one string of 256 KiB can take up to 2.3 seconds) the strings the evidence supplied are no longer judged: each is replaced whole by <withheld N bytes: backstop: the judging time ran out>, counted and listed, and the answer is partial, except the names this tool wrote itself (its keys, the names of its result files, the name of the input, its status basis) and a string of 15 characters or fewer made only of letters, digits, _ and . that does not start like a vendor token and, in a field of a typed kind (a SID, a GUID, a digest), fits the grammar of its type (so not a Slack-shaped token, not the value after a flag such as -pwd, not a prefix and 12 characters). The seal stop ends the judging only, not the tool's own work, which has its own, earlier clock. When any part of a free-text string is withheld, the line breaks, tabs and invisible characters of that string are not kept in the text shown (it is judged without them); a string with nothing withheld is shown exactly as it is. Binary data written as hexadecimal is decoded and judged by its printable text, by both layers and by the backstop on its own; hexadecimal with no secret-shaped text in it is shown as it is, random bytes included (a binary key is printed). A filter on content (contains) is applied to the text the answer prints (after the layers and the backstop), never to what either withheld or replaced: what it did not match and has text withheld in it is counted (contains_blind_records) and makes the answer partial, because the needle may be in what is withheld; the count is the same whatever the needle is. write_values: true writes the originals of everything withheld to <tool>-values.jsonl (mode 0600, created first, never replaced) and is accepted only in a job the harness runs as secret output (the manifest declares it; SECRET_OUTPUT=1), refused as JSON anywhere else before anything is made. EventData fields are typed by name (SID, GUID, hash, address, time, path and registry key fields); every other field is free text. Measured on random plants of every shape in 13 slots (988 per shape, five independent runs, 4,940 per shape; rates, not guarantees; the tests plant them again): prefixed tokens (GitHub, GitLab, Stripe, SendGrid, Google, npm, AWS key ids), JWT, PEM keys (one line and several), connection strings, user-info (an @, a / or a + inside the password, a random user of any length, a GitLab token glued to hexadecimal digits), NUL, zero-width and full-width splits, upper-case and glued prefixes: 0 printed whole in 4,940 plants of each shape and no piece of 12 characters of one printed; AWS-shaped secret keys of 40 characters: about 0.1% printed whole (0 whole and 1 piece of 12 characters in 4,940 plants of the block's own harness; 1 of 105 canaries end to end, the same canary in four slots; an earlier measurement found 2 whole and 3 pieces in 4,940), so the rate is small and not zero. The shapes that are not zero, as the range of the five runs over all slots with the worst single slot (76 plants, one plant is 1.3%) beside it: 16, 20 and 32-byte base64 keys 0.0% to 0.3% (worst slot 1.3%; up to 3.9% in end-to-end runs); random base62 of 20 to 40 characters 0.0% to 0.3% (worst slot 2.6%); random lower-case letters of 24 9.2% to 10.6% (worst slot 14.5% to 21.1%); a 16-character base32 seed 9.8% to 11.7% (worst slot 15.8% to 21.1%). In a binary slot (a hexadecimal REG_BINARY value or table cell) the backstop decodes the hexadecimal and replaces every hex-encoded shape it claims (480 of 480 plants), but random bytes that hold no text are printed (200 of 200), and so is a hexadecimal secret written as text there (a 32-digit one in a table cell: 97%). Strings changed (any part withheld) on real evidence: in a real 72 MB SOFTWARE hive (3,000 strings sampled per class) 3.7% of key-name components, 1.0% of value names and 0.9% of REG_SZ data (the names of the Windows component store, WinSxS, are not replaced by the backstop in a name, key or path); in real event logs (175 logs, 64,716 records, up to 4 MB each) the XML of 2.0% of the records is replaced whole by the backstop (5.6% before the shape guard of this round; Security 0.1%, was 6.7%), 1.7% of the data fields are withheld (3.7% before, process ids no longer) and 45 of the 175 runs end partial (84 before). The average hides channels: PowerShell/Operational has the XML of 25.0% of its 1,857 records replaced whole (script blocks carry base64 and long identifiers) and CodeIntegrity/Operational 33.3% of its 1,309 (event 3089, whose Hash is a padded base64 digest). Strings the shape rules change that are not secrets: numbers of 19 digits or more (handles, a Chrome field-trial handle, a mojo pipe name), unlabelled hexadecimal runs of 32 digits or more (the native-image directories), and the query values of a URL in a URL slot. NOT recognised, by design: a secret that does not look like one (a plain password or passphrase, a pronounceable passphrase, a UUID-shaped key, a hexadecimal secret of up to 24 digits in a name or of any length in a binary slot, anything under 16 characters in a name; 69% to 100% of such plants are printed): withholding is by shape, so a file whose secrets matter is read in a job run with secret_output: true.

event_ids.description: Optional list of numeric event IDs to include

contains.description: Optional case-insensitive substring that must appear in the XML; the text is looked at as shown, so a needle inside withheld text matches nothing and what it did not match but has text withheld is counted and makes the answer partial

limit.description: Events shown inline (default 200, an inline page size); every matching event and its XML as the boundary shows it (a withheld text is a placeholder; the log holds the whole record) is kept in result_file, and parse-error rows are listed under errors and kept there too

out_file.description: Optional JSONL result path under the run (in a job, under $OUT); defaults to work/<your id>/tool-output/ (in a job, $OUT). An existing file is never replaced: the first free name beside it is used and named

start_time.description: Optional ISO 8601 lower bound on the XML's SystemTime: the beginning of the span the text names (2026-09-01 is 00:00 that day, 2026-09-01T10:00 is 10:00:00); no zone is UTC, Z or an offset is applied

end_time.description: Optional ISO 8601 upper bound on the XML's SystemTime: the end of the span the text names, so 2026-09-01 includes the whole day and 2026-09-01T10:00 that whole minute; no zone is UTC, Z or an offset is applied

write_values.description: Write the originals of everything the boundary withheld to a file under $OUT (mode 0600, created first, never replaced): only in a job run with secret_output: true, refused anywhere else; default false
